body:
Confirmed. Doesn't affect Vim. 

Does it happen in Nvim 0.3.0 or earlier?
I can't say. I know that I only got this issue after I updated my packages, but I can't recall if I was using 0.3.0 or 0.2.2.
I can verify that this bug does not exist in 0.2.2, I have not tried 0.3.0.

I tried to debug and traced it to 
```
msg_puts_attr_len (str=0x7fe738c9bfb0 "\ntest\n[O]k: ", len=-1, attr=23)
    at ../src/nvim/message.c:1631
```
with 
```
  // Don't print anything when using ":silent cmd".                                                                                                                            
  if (msg_silent != 0) {                                                                                                                                                       
    return;                                                                                                                                                                    
  } 
```
and 
```
(gdb) p msg_silent
$10 = 1
```

@MichaHoffmann Thanks, that's expected, but the question is why `msg_silent` is non-zero? https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/8840 is related I guess (I have a PR for that one, but it seems like something more general changed... need to bisect to the commit that caused this.) https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/8840#issuecomment-412145577 was bisected to `shortmess=F` default, but I don't think that's the cause of this one.

Okay, i'll bisect this one in the afternoon, if it helps!

edit: 
bisected this to `b7514493a0c4a4389a5921f15b0b429dae5c75e7 is the first bad commit`; that seems to be the `shortmess=F` one.

edit2: :set shortmess=a on this commit results in the expected behaviour again too.

Problem:    Segfault when pattern with \z() is very slow.
Solution:   Check for NULL regprog.  Add "nfa_fail" to test_override() to be
            able to test this.  Fix that 'searchhl' resets called_emsg.
https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/bcf9442307075bac40d44328c8bf7ea21857b138

closes #8788
